title: JSON on the Command Line: jq & az --query

scenes.line2: How do you script with it?
scenes.say: Cloud tools spit out JSON everywhere. But how do you actually use that in your scripts?

scenes.label: jq
scenes.sub: jq filters and reshapes JSON from any command.
scenes.say: First up: jq. It's your Swiss Army knife for slicing and dicing JSON right in the terminal.

scenes.title: Filter API and k8s output
scenes.say: You can pull just what you need from API responses or Kubernetes with simple jq filters.

scenes.label: az --query
scenes.sub: az uses JMESPath to filter JSON from Azure.
scenes.say: For Azure, use az dash dash query. It speaks JMESPath, a powerful JSON query language.

scenes.title: Filter Azure VM & NSG rules
scenes.say: With az, you can filter for running VMs or allowed network rules, all before the data hits your script.

scenes.question: How should you parse JSON in bash?
scenes.wrong: Just grep for the values you need.
scenes.right: Use jq or az --query. Grep breaks easily and isn't safe for JSON.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Don't ever grep JSON. Always use jq or az dash dash query. Grep will break and miss edge cases.
